name: Paraneoplastic Pemphigus

criteria.description: Severe mucositis with polymorphous skin eruptions including blisters and erosions
Presence of an underlying neoplasm, commonly lymphoproliferative disorders
Detection of circulating autoantibodies against plakin family proteins by immunoprecipitation or immunoblotting
Histological evidence of acantholysis and interface dermatitis on skin biopsy
Intercellular and basement membrane zone deposition of IgG and complement on direct immunofluorescence

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe mucocutaneous lesions, underlying neoplasm, and circulating autoantibodies against plakin proteins
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, and immunological findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe painful mucositis involving oral mucosa
Polymorphous blistering skin eruptions with erosions
searchTerms: varied blistering skin rash with sores
bronchiolitis obliterans caused by immune attack

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to esophageal mucosal involvement

searchTerms: nail deformities and surrounding skin infection
low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count

rare.symptomName: Severe respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation

laboratory: Circulating autoantibodies against plakin family proteins (envoplakin, periplakin)
imaging: Chest CT showing bronchiolitis obliterans with air trapping and bronchiectasis
Radiologic evidence of underlying neoplasm (e.g., lymphoma)
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; autoimmune etiology
other: Skin biopsy showing acantholysis and interface dermatitis
Direct immunofluorescence with IgG and complement deposition

distinguishingFeatures: Less severe mucositis and absence of bronchiolitis obliterans
Tense blisters rather than polymorphous lesions
Autoantibodies against hemidesmosomal proteins BP180 and BP230
Target lesions with less severe mucosal involvement
Usually triggered by infections or drugs

redFlags: Rapidly progressive mucosal erosions refractory to standard therapies
Development of bronchiolitis obliterans causing respiratory compromise
Presence of underlying malignancy requiring oncologic evaluation
references: Camisa C, Helm TN. Paraneoplastic pemphigus: a clinical and immunopathologic study of 20 patients. Medicine (Baltimore). 1993.
Anhalt GJ et al. Paraneoplastic pemphigus: an autoimmune mucocutaneous disease associated with neoplasia. N Engl J Med. 1990.
Nguyen VT, et al. Paraneoplastic pemphigus: clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2018.
